_fixture: what .claude/skills/apply-job/scan-page.js produces for pages/lever.html — GENERATED by running the real scanner over the served page, never hand-written
_bridge: tests/security/scan-fidelity.test.mjs runs the REAL scanner over that HTML and deep-compares this file to its output. Edit one and the other goes red.
_why: bench-apply.mjs's board resolver THREW for `--board lever`, so the one board in the corpus with a NATIVE <select> — options already in the DOM, where probing is pure waste — could not be measured against the two where probing is unavoidable. Phase 0.10.
_finding_g1: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING g1. The sponsorship question's group label is "Yes" — the first radio's own option text — NOT "Will you now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status? ✱", which is the question a human sees. Lever puts that text in a <div class="application-label"> SIBLING of the <ul>, and scan-page.js's wrapping-<label> tier wins before the four-ancestor class walk can reach it, so the group takes the label of the control it wraps. `labelWhy` records that more than one control shares it. This is not fixture drift and must not be 'corrected' here: it is what the scanner produces for the commonest yes/no rendering on a real ATS, and the fixture's job is to say so. Filed against w2-engine; the consumer-level assertion is in tests/security/board-fidelity.test.mjs.
_g2_consent: The privacy-policy tickbox is a single-option checkbox GROUP (g2) with `labelExact`. It is the shape rule 6 defers on regardless of topic — a checkbox carries assent, not a value.
_k_order: No combos on this page, so the stamp order IS reading order (f1..f10) and the two groups g1/g2 are minted after the inputs they contain. Contrast greenhouse-step1 and ashby-step1, where a combo takes f1.
